PE1-09.hint: Point-slope form is \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\). With two points, find the slope first. The point on the \(y\)-axis gives the intercept directly.
slips: Putting the point's coordinates in the wrong places, for example \(y - 2 = -3(x + 5)\).
Subtracting the coordinates in a different order on the top and the bottom of the slope.
PE1-09.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

PE1-10.hint: Solve for \(y\) so the equation looks like \(y = mx + b\). Divide every term, including the right side, by the coefficient of \(y\).
slips: Reading the slope as \(5\) straight from the equation. This is standard form, not slope-intercept form.
Dividing only some terms by \(2\). The \(14\) must be divided too.
Losing the sign when moving \(5x\) to the other side.
PE1-10.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

parts.q: Write in point-slope form the line with slope \(-3\) through \((2,-5)\).
Write in slope-intercept form the line through \((0,4)\) and \((3,13)\).
Determine the slope and \(y\)-intercept of the line \(5x + 2y = 14\).
parts.a: Solve for \(y\): \(2y = -5x + 14\), so \(y = -\dfrac{5}{2}x + 7\). The slope is \(-\dfrac{5}{2}\) and the \(y\)-intercept is \((0,7)\).
